text:
mira: Quick thread - we need a clean policy for customers who want to upgrade tiers mid-billing-cycle and expect prorated credits. What's the safe product + contract approach?

anika: Two main asks from sales: 1) immediate tier activation on purchase, 2) automatic prorate credit applied to next invoice. Ops + Finance worry about usage spikes and revenue recognition.

kevin: Sales perspective: customers expect 'instant upgrade' without disruption. We can grant immediate active tier but limit revert/backfill windows. Suggest: upgrade effective immediately, prorate credit posted to next invoice, but temporary grace capacity limited to 14 days or X compute units.

ops_lee: Implementation constraints: if we allow immediate tier change, we must enforce a grace cap so ops doesn't get surprised. Proposed knobs: grace_days, grace_unit_cap, enforcement: cap per-route and per-account, alert at 60/90%. Also need an emergency throttle if pooled capacity > threshold.

legal_sam: Contractly, avoid language that implies refunds beyond the posted credit. Suggested blurb: "Upgrades become effective immediately. Redwood will apply a prorated credit toward future invoices; such credits are non-refundable. Temporary uplift capacity (grace capacity) is for operational convenience and does not constitute a guaranteed service level unless an SLA addendum is executed."

finance_zoe: For GAAP we need a consistent policy: prorated credits should be recorded as contra-revenue when applied, not as refunds. If we offer extended grace (>30d) treat as a separate commercial arrangement. Also need invoice preview in checkout to avoid disputes.

kevin: Commercial flow idea: three options at purchase - Instant Upgrade (grace cap 14d), Scheduled Upgrade (effective at next billing cycle, no grace), and Trial Bump (time-limited promo credit applied with approval). Sales can pick.

mira: Product config example (short):

```yaml
upgrade_policy:
  default:
    grace_days: 14
    grace_units: 50000
    emergency_reclaimable: true
  scheduled:
    effective_at_next_cycle: true
  trial_bump:
    approval_required: true
    expiry_days: 30
```

anika: UX: clearly show "grace capacity" and expiry in the console and on invoice preview. Also add a checkbox: "I accept that temporary uplift is non-guaranteed and may be reclaimed".

ops_lee: We'll add telemetry: upgrade events, grace consumption per-customer, and a weekly report for capacity planning. Also add a hard throttle override for SRE on call.

billing-bot: Ticket BILL-3310 created: implement upgrade_proration UI + invoice_preview + grace flags. Owner=billing-team, due=2025-06-01.

kevin: Last piece: escalation for permanent tier changes with SLA should go through Sales Director -> Legal -> VP. Document the approval path.

mira: I'll put together a one-pager with the options + UI mock + contract snippet and circulate for sign-off. Target: draft by Wed.

anika: Thanks — please include sample language for the pricing page and checkout flows so marketing can update copy.
